parts.markdown:
Use our free **Mississippi paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Mississippi income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Mississippi's income tax system allows employees to benefit from personal exemptions, standard deductions and a zero-rate taxable income threshold. Understanding these adjustments can help you estimate your earnings more accurately.

Whether you work in Jackson, Gulfport, Southaven, Hattiesburg or another Mississippi community, this calculator can help you compare employment opportunities and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the Mississippi Paycheck Calculator

Start by choosing whether you receive a fixed annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross income before taxes and select your payment frequency. Hourly employees should include regular working hours and qualifying overtime hours.

Enter the federal and Mississippi income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions and healthcare premiums. Enter the full tax amounts, including extra tax your employer withheld.

Review your estimated gross earnings, individual tax deductions and remaining take-home pay.

For greater accuracy, use information from your latest pay stub and withholding certificates rather than estimating your current deductions.

## How Mississippi State Income Tax Works

Mississippi applies a 4% individual income tax rate to applicable taxable income above $10,000 in 2026.

The first $10,000 of taxable income is subject to a zero rate.

However, taxable income is not necessarily the same as your annual gross salary.

Mississippi's withholding methodology accounts for applicable personal exemptions and standard deductions before calculating the amount subject to state income tax.

For example, an employee earning $40,000 annually may have substantially less than $40,000 in income subject to the 4% rate.

A reliable Mississippi salary calculator must account for the applicable deductions rather than simply multiplying gross wages by 4%.

## Understanding Mississippi Form 89-350

Mississippi employees generally provide withholding information through Form 89-350, the Employee's Withholding Exemption Certificate.

The form allows employees to communicate their applicable personal exemptions and additional withholding information to their employers.

Your Mississippi withholding elections are separate from your federal Form W-4.

Employees with more than one job or married employees whose spouses also work should review their exemption allocations carefully.

Claiming the full household exemption independently at multiple jobs could result in insufficient withholding.

Current withholding forms and instructions are available through the Mississippi Department of Revenue.

## Mississippi Income Tax Calculation Example

Consider a single employee earning $65,000 annually before taxes.

Assume the employee qualifies for the standard single personal exemption and standard deduction, has no additional dependents and has no other taxable wage adjustments.

Annual taxable wages: $65,000

Personal exemption: $6,000

Standard deduction: $2,300

Adjusted annual income:

$65,000 − $6,000 − $2,300 = $56,700

Subtract the zero-rate taxable income threshold:

$56,700 − $10,000 = $46,700

Illustrative annualized withholding:

$46,700 × 4% = $1,868

Dividing this amount across 26 biweekly pay periods gives approximately $71.85 before applicable employer rounding.

The actual amount withheld may differ depending on the authorized withholding method and your exemption certificate.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Mississippi Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable earnings, filing status, payment frequency and Form W-4 information.

Employees with multiple jobs, other sources of income or eligible tax credits may require additional withholding adjustments.

Review [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) for official federal withholding procedures.

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered earnings toward Social Security.

The annual taxable wage ceiling is $184,500 in 2026.

An employee receiving $2,500 in covered wages before reaching the annual limit would contribute $155.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when Medicare-covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

The [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) explains these federal payroll requirements.

## Mississippi Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate gross earnings using their hourly wage and working hours.

Suppose an employee earns $23 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours paid at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$23 × 40 = $920

Overtime earnings:

$23 × 1.5 × 6 = $207

Total gross earnings:

$1,127

Applicable federal and Mississippi income tax withholding and payroll contributions are then calculated from the relevant taxable wage amounts.

Consult the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about overtime eligibility and exemptions.

## Mississippi Paycheck Tax Threshold Example

Consider a single employee with $18,300 in annual taxable wages before applicable Mississippi deductions.

Subtracting the $6,000 personal exemption and $2,300 standard deduction leaves $10,000.

Under the ordinary 2026 tax schedule, that amount falls entirely within the zero-rate range.

However, this does not eliminate federal income tax or payroll contributions where applicable.

It also does not mean every employee earning $18,300 automatically qualifies for identical withholding treatment. Exemption elections and employment circumstances matter.

## Does Mississippi Have Local Income Taxes?

Mississippi municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes on ordinary employee compensation.

Employees still pay applicable federal and Mississippi income taxes and ordinary payroll contributions.

Local sales taxes, housing costs, insurance premiums and transportation expenses can affect household purchasing power but should be evaluated separately from payroll deductions.

## Comparing Salaries in Mississippi

When comparing employment offers, consider estimated net earnings alongside the value of employee benefits.

Retirement matching, healthcare premiums, paid leave and commuting expenses can influence the overall financial value of a job.

An employee receiving a higher gross salary may not necessarily experience an equally large improvement in disposable income.

Use the calculator to compare different employment offers, and then evaluate essential household expenses.

Our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare compensation arrangements, while our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a suitable savings target.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Mississippi's income tax rate in 2026?

Mississippi applies a 4% rate to applicable taxable income exceeding $10,000. Personal exemptions, standard deductions and withholding elections affect the amount withheld from your paycheck.

### Does Mississippi tax every dollar of my salary?

No. Applicable exemptions, deductions and the zero-rate threshold can reduce the amount subject to state income tax.

### Does Mississippi have municipal employee income taxes?

Mississippi municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes. Applicable federal and state taxes still reduce employee earnings.
